newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss experts oppose Scientology surveillance.
newsitem.headline: Swiss experts oppose Scientology surveillance.

text.p: Switzerland does not need to follow Germany's example and put the Church of Scientology under surveillance by federal police, a Swiss Justice Ministry advisory panel said on Tuesday.
It said in a statement that Scientology "does not pose a direct and urgent danger to Swiss domestic security," a criterion that the group would have to meet to warrant observation by federal police.
The Swiss experts said their findings would not be final until Scientology supporters and critics were able to comment on a report drawn up by a working group of the committee.

"But the working group found that the activity of Scientology appears questionable in many circles and can be connected with risks and high financial expenditures for the (Scientology) members," the committee said.

"There are indications that Scientology operates a comprehensive intelligence service," it said, added that this was aimed mainly at collecting information about members and critics rather than about the state.

The Justice Ministry could either accept the findings by the Consultative Committee on Protecting the State, a standing body of experts which advises the ministry, or it could act on its own, a ministry spokesman said.
Germany's 16 regional states said on Friday that sufficient suspicion existed of anti-democratic intent by Scientology to merit surveillance by anti-extremist state and federal watchdogs.

Scientology, based in Los Angeles, was founded in 1954 and based on the teachings of science fiction writer L. Ron Hubbard. Its members take personality tests and are then offered courses and literature to help them to realise what the group believes is their full potential.
Germany argues that Scientology is purely an economic organisation which exploits the insecurities of its members to extract big profits from the self-improvement courses.
The group has accused Germany of persecuting it and its members and of mounting an "hysterical witchhunt" against it at taxpayers' expense.
